newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: SLOVAK CENTRAL BANK CALLS FOR GRADUAL BANK SELLOFF.
newsitem.headline: SLOVAK CENTRAL BANK CALLS FOR GRADUAL BANK SELLOFF.

text.p: The National Bank of Slovakia on Friday (NBS) said the full privatisation of the country's largest banks should occur only after their restructuring has been completed.

"We think the privatisation of the largest banks should proceed gradually and that the state should keep its control in these banks until the banking sector has been completely restructured," NBS Vice-governor Jozef Mudrik told a conference.
Mudrik said that under ideal conditions, the restructuring process could be completed within about three years. "There are several conditions for the ideal procedure of restruturing," he said.
"These include changes to current legislation which taxes reserves for classified loans and requires that the interest income from such credits be included in their profit," he said.

This, however, could cost the state buget some eight billion crowns over the three years, Mudrik said. "But once restructuring is completed, the state budget would profit by some four to six billion crowns a year", he added.
He said that much depends on the utilisation of a two billion crown state assistance plan for restructuring bank loan portfolios which is included in the 1997 budget draft.
"The NBS is of the opinion that money would be better used to cover the changes in legislation," Mudrik said.
If the NBS proposals are not adopted, the entire restructuring process could take some four to five years, he warned.
"In this case the central bank would press the commercial banks to solve their restructuring problems from their own resources, such as through subordinated debt issues," he said.
Some Slovak banks are already negotiating conditions for such an instrument, he said, adding that if they succeed restructuring would take less time.

One subordinated debt has already been signed by the Tatra Banka., the largest commercial bank, and the largest saving bank Slovenska Sporitelna are negotiating similar instruments which are subject to NBS approval.

Restructuring and privatisation of the four major Slovak financial institutions, VUB and IRB bank, Slovenska Sporitelna and the largest insurer Slovenska Poistovna, is considered crucial for further economic reform and acceptance of Slovakia to western economic structures.
The privatisation process has, however, been postponed by law until the end of March 1997.
